messages:
incident-bot: Incident created — Canary health failures detected for rollout 'wave-7' in us-west-2. Severity: P2. Pager: @Maya Patel. Alerts: elevated 5xx rate on /health and increased latency.

Maya: I'm on it. seeing spike ~12:34 UTC. 5xx ~18% from the canary group 'edge-v2'. baseline was ~0.4%.

Jason: Jumping into cluster now. Which deployment/version?

Ben: rollout id: roll-2026-03-15-wave7, image: rwd-inference/edge:release-20260315. Canary percentage ~10% currently.

Maya: Logs show liveness probe failures, restarts on some pods. Noticing GC pauses in the logs too.

Jason: I see this in pod logs:
```
[2026-03-15T12:33:24Z] ERROR: failed health check: tcp_connect: connection reset
[2026-03-15T12:33:26Z] WARN: kv-cache OOM, clearing cache, mem before: 6.8GB
[2026-03-15T12:33:28Z] INFO: restarting process due to liveness probe failure
```

Ben: Are these only canaries? Any control/old-model traffic seeing it?

Maya: Control pool (edge-v1) looks fine. Only edge-v2 canary pods. No broader regions impacted yet.

Anil: @Maya can you check the deploy config—maybe new feature flag/quantization profile triggered?

Maya: On it. Checking flags for this rollout: 'edge_v2_enable' = true, 'kv_cache_mode' = "aggressive", quantization_profile = q4_0.

Ben: Aggressive kv cache + q4_0 on smaller memory instances could cause OOM-ish behavior. We had a ticket warning about that.

Maya: Customer impact: internal smoke tests failing; a small subset of requests from some PLG customers are getting 502/503s. Support notified. No enterprise Dedicated tenants reporting errors yet (checked last 10m).

Jason: Recommend kill-switch the feature flag for canary immediately to stop roll forward. We can either reduce canary % or flip the flag.

Maya: Agreed. I'll toggle the flag to false for canary group. Command:
```bash
# admin API toggle
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://flags.redwood.internal/api/toggle \
  -d '{"flag":"edge_v2_enable","env":"canary","value":false}'
```

deploy-bot: Received request to toggle flag 'edge_v2_enable' for env=canary. Executing...

deploy-bot: Flag toggle succeeded. edge_v2_enable=false on canary (propagated to 100% canary nodes).

Maya: Watching metrics. 5xx rate dropping — good sign. Latency trending down.

Ben: I'll keep an eye on pod restarts. If restarts continue, we should roll back the image.

Jason: On pod list now — rolling restart seems to stabilize after flag flip. Pods not failing liveness any more.

Maya: Support update: sent quick note to affected customers; PS team prepping follow-up. No SLA breaches expected but we’ll monitor.

Anil: Can we snapshot the canary pods logs and heap profiles for postmortem before any restart? Need to capture evidence of kv-cache/OOM.

Maya: Done — collected pprof and logs to gs://redwood-incidents/wave7/2473001234.

Ben: Next steps: revert aggressive kv_cache_mode for the canary config and re-run load tests in staging. Also open a revert/rollback candidate in case the flag flip didn't help.

Jason: I'll create a quick revert: set image back to release-20260314 on the canary subset if necessary.

Maya: For now, canary health metrics look back to baseline. I'll un-page oncall rotation in 20m once we confirm 15m stable. Marking incident as mitigated.

Anil: Thanks. Handing off to night oncall @Anil Rao — summary: canary wave-7 caused liveness failures due to aggressive kv cache + q4_0 profile on memory-constrained hosts. Mitigation: feature flag kill-switch toggled (edge_v2_enable=false), logs/pprof captured, support notified. Watch list: any re-deploy that re-enables the flag, pods that restart >3x in 5m, and errors for PLG customers.

Maya: @Anil attaching quick commands and links:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/edge/canary-wave7
- Logs: https://logs.redwood/internal/query?incident=2473001234
- Flag API: https://flags.redwood.internal/docs

Anil: Got it. I'll monitor overnight and escalate if any regression.

Maya: Closing thread from mitigation side. Will create postmortem draft tomorrow and link here. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident mitigated and put into 'postmortem-required' state. Incident ID: INC-2026-03-15-2473001234.

Jason: quick note for postmortem — include threshold tuning for canary health, and add an automatic rollback if liveness restarts > 5 within 10m.

Ben: Also add a preflight check for kv_cache_mode vs instance type (memory). Patch assigned to eng-runtime.

Maya: Thanks team — good catch and fast work.
